review_notes: I read the whole file and the other files in Ends/ (Properties.lean) to check uses of the hom/supp API. I grepped Mathlib for uses of hom_refl, hom_trans, hom_mk and componentComplMk_mem. I could not run Lean. Whether a simp lemma stated through the `abbrev` `ComponentCompl.hom` gets a usable discrimination-tree key is unverified, and so is whether `simp` would close the `map_comp` goal without `hom_trans`. The findings are therefore proposals, not observed simp failures. I did not find any rewrite loops. I considered the `@[simp]` on `mem_supp_iff` (it unfolds membership into an existential) and the dual `C.supp` / `(C : Set V)` spellings, but I had no use showing a practical problem, so I did not report them.

findings.excerpt: theorem hom_refl (C : G.ComponentCompl L) : C.hom (subset_refl L) = C := by
findings.problem: `hom_refl` is the identity law for the transition maps. It is a normalising rewrite: the right-hand side is strictly simpler and the proof argument is irrelevant. It is not tagged `@[simp]`. The only use in the library, the `map_id` field of `componentComplFunctor`, passes it by hand as `simp [ComponentCompl.hom_refl]`. Every client that simplifies `C.hom (subset_refl L)` or `C.hom le_rfl` has to repeat that.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `hom_refl` `@[simp]`, and then drop the explicit argument at line 266 (`simp`). Because `hom` is an `abbrev` for `ConnectedComponent.map ...`, the discrimination-tree key unfolds to `map`. If that key turns out to be too general or too specific, state the lemma in terms of an arbitrary proof `h : L ⊆ L` instead of `subset_refl L`.
findings.benefit: The `ComponentCompl.hom` functoriality interface (identity law, with `hom_trans` as the composition law) gets a canonical simp normal form. `map_id`-style goals, and the same goals in downstream end-related files, close with plain `simp` and no hand-supplied lemma.

findings.excerpt:
theorem hom_mk {v : V} (vnL : v ∉ L) (h : K ⊆ L) :
    (G.componentComplMk vnL).hom h = G.componentComplMk (Set.notMem_subset h vnL) :=
  rfl
findings.problem: `hom_mk` is the evaluation rule for `hom` on a component given by a vertex. It is the standard way to reduce `(componentComplMk v).hom h` to `componentComplMk v`, but it carries no simp attribute. `end_hom_mk_of_mk` applies it by hand, and `hom_trans`/`hom_refl` have no accompanying simp normal form for `hom` either. The lemma is `rfl`, so it terminates and each application strictly removes a `hom`. A user whose goal contains `(G.componentComplMk vnL).hom h` therefore has no automatic way to reduce it, and the transition-map API has no simp-normal form for vertex-built components.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `hom_mk`. Consider also `@[simp]` on `hom_refl` (see the other finding). Leave `hom_trans` un-simp: its right-hand side is not obviously simpler, and orienting it either way could compete with `hom_mk`. Then `end_hom_mk_of_mk` can finish with `simp` or `exact hom_mk ..`.
findings.benefit: `hom` applied to vertex-built components reduces to a vertex-built component automatically. Proofs about sections of `componentComplFunctor` that currently need `apply ComponentCompl.hom_mk` or `rfl` would not need those hand steps.
